The disclosure is material to this round because PTCB-V44-S2 below is the recurrence of that same failure mode one generation deeper, and because at v43 I checked the vector roster against the immediately preceding requirement rather than against the accumulated set. shouldFix.title: The repair of PTCB-V43-S1 omits the zero-linux_banner vector that the finding it answers explicitly enumerated, and the subject's own repair note concedes the omission
evidence: The governing rule has two distinct refuse branches. /loaderTraces/objectAuthenticityBind/tags/linux-pathless/measuredBootBind/kexecAbsenceDerivation/builderAttestation/kernelReleaseParse reads verbatim: 'Zero or more than one linux_banner refuses.' Zero-banner and multiple-banner are separate failure conditions of a uniqueness predicate, reachable by different payloads.

The v44 roster names only one of the two. Splitting /g22/ikconfigParserVectors on ';' yields exactly 47 named vectors; vector 8 is 'multiple linux_banner refuse'. No vector names the zero-linux_banner refuse branch.

Frozen Codex v43 PTCB-V43-S1 requiredRepair enumerated the branch by name: 'Preserve distinct vectors for wrong memberSha256, altered kexecCapability, payloadDigest mismatch, zero and duplicate builderRoot, zero and multiple linux_banner, present non-32-byte key, ...'. Every other item on that enumeration is delivered in v44 (memberSha256 vector 3, kexecCapability 4, payloadDigest 5, absent builderRoot 6, duplicate builderRoot 7, non-32-byte key 9, correctly encoded invalid signature 11, loaded-section accept 24, zero-marker absent branch 28). 'zero ... linux_banner' is the single enumerated item not delivered.

The subject concedes the gap in the same sentence that claims the repair. /honestyRepairsFromV43/[0] reads: 'zero linux_banner is already covered only if named - multiple linux_banner refuse'. That states the coverage condition ('only if named') and then names only the multiple branch. It is not a withdrawal and not a coverage claim; it is an acknowledgement that the branch is uncovered.

The subject's own appended guidance names this as an attack target. /reviewGuidance/forTheIndependentReviewer/[221], added by v44, instructs: 'Attack a G22 roster that ... drops ... linux_banner uniqueness ...'. Uniqueness is exactly-one; a roster that tests only the more-than-one side tests half the predicate.

The literal union claim is separately true and does not rescue this. v41, v42 and v43 rosters each named only 'multiple linux_banner', so the v42-union-v43 set genuinely excludes zero-banner. That is why the narrower restatement in /honestyRepairsFromV43 ('union of every v42 required vector and every v43 addition') passes while Codex's actual requiredRepair does not: the repair was scoped to the union rather than to the enumerated list of distinct vectors the finding demanded.
shouldFix.impact: A G22 implementation can satisfy all 47 named vectors while never exercising kernelReleaseParse against a payload P containing no linux_banner. That is the fail-open side of the uniqueness predicate: builderAttestation.preimage.kernelRelease is a signed field that must be checked against a release parsed out of P, and the zero-match case is where a parser most plausibly returns empty, default, or unchecked rather than refusing. PTCB-V43-S1 is therefore recorded as repaired while one of its named required vectors remains unnamed.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add a distinct named vector 'zero linux_banner refuse' to /g22/ikconfigParserVectors alongside the existing 'multiple linux_banner refuse', so the roster covers both branches of kernelReleaseParse's uniqueness predicate. Replace the concessive clause in /honestyRepairsFromV43/[0] with a plain statement that both branches are named. If the author instead intends the zero branch to be out of roster scope, that requires a named semantic withdrawal under /g22/vectorRosterRule, which no version has issued and which the live kernelReleaseParse text contradicts.

shouldFix.title: vectorRosterRule is declared GOVERNING over every predecessor required vector, but the roster it governs is satisfied only across v42 and v43, leaving v37-v40 required vectors dropped with no named semantic withdrawal
evidence: The rule is unrestricted as to generation. /g22/vectorRosterRule reads: 'GOVERNING. Successor required-vector rosters are cumulative. Every predecessor required vector remains required unless a named semantic withdrawal makes it obsolete.' 'Cumulative' and 'every predecessor' cannot mean only the immediate predecessor: a rule scoped to one generation permits one vector to be dropped per version indefinitely while every single step remains 'cumulative', which is the precise erosion the rule exists to prevent.

The roster satisfies a narrower scope than the rule asserts. /g22/ikconfigParserVectors is captioned 'union of v42 and v43', and /g22/vectorRosterRule closes with 'No vector from v42 or v43 is withdrawn here.' Neither the caption nor the closing sentence addresses v37, v38, v39 or v40, and no sentence anywhere in the subject withdraws a vector from those rosters.

Those earlier rosters exist and named required vectors. g22.ikconfigParserVectors is present from v37 onward: v37 'Required classes: ... raw-PE decoy pair ignored/refused; duplicate pairs refuse; omitted requiredN refuses; unsupported compression refuses; malformed setup_header refuses; malformed zimg refuses'; v38 'Also required: PE entrypoint-bypass decoy payload refuses; ... six-line IKCONFIG decoy refuses; signed ikconfigDigest mismatch refuses; ... arm64 duplicate zimg refuses; compressed_type/magic disagreement refuses'; v39 'Required: ... arm64 magic-free section refuses; compressed_type/magic disagreement refuses; concatenated gzip refuses'.

The dropped vectors are not obsolete, because the rules they test are still live and normative in v44. kconfigSerialization.complete: 'A six-line decoy refuses.' and 'Duplicate CONFIG_NAME refuses.' kconfigSerialization.disabledForm: 'Omission is not disabled. =y or =m refuses.' architectureDispatch['linux/arm64'].zimgDecision: 'More than one refuses.' architectureDispatch['linux/arm64'].zboot: 'compressed_type MUST equal decompress.detect. ... Disagreement refuses.' architectureDispatch['linux/arm64'].uncompressedImage: 'No magic-free fallback.' decompress.detect: 'Other magics refuse as unsupported-compression.' decompress.cLimit: 'Concatenated extra gzip members after the first refuse. Trailing non-gzip bytes after that member refuse.' ikconfig.presentBranch: 'signedObject.ikconfigDigest MUST equal result.ikconfigDigest.'

The subject's own live reviewGuidance still directs attacks at exactly these uncovered cases. [186]: 'Attack an IKCONFIG search that still accepts a raw-PE decoy pair, omitted requiredN as n, or more than one marker pair.' [192]: 'Attack an IKCONFIG that is still a six-line decoy or still unsigned as the config that compiled the member.' [198]: 'Attack an arm64 magic-free fallback ...'. A required-vector roster that omits what the artifact's own guidance names as the standing attacks is not cumulative in any useful sense.

Mechanical membership test against the 47-vector v44 roster: raw-PE decoy pair ABSENT; omitted requiredN ABSENT; six-line IKCONFIG decoy ABSENT; arm64 magic-free fallback ABSENT; compressed_type/magic disagreement ABSENT; concatenated gzip / trailing bytes ABSENT; arm64 duplicate zimg ABSENT (the five 'zimg' hits are all arm64-zimg-loaded headerKind mapping vectors, not a zimg-cardinality vector); signed ikconfigDigest mismatch ABSENT; unsupported compression ABSENT; malformed setup_header and malformed zimg ABSENT; PE entrypoint-bypass decoy payload ABSENT.

The withdrawal mechanism demonstrably works when used, which shows these omissions are unaccounted rather than intentional. v39's 'forbidden symbol present refuses' IS properly obsolete: kexecSymbolAbsence.standing reads 'WITHDRAWN as structural proof', and honestyRepairsFromV39/[0] records 'raw UTF-8 symbol-name scan is withdrawn as structural proof'. That is the named semantic withdrawal the rule contemplates. No comparable sentence exists for any vector listed above.
shouldFix.impact: This is the recurrence of PTCB-V43-S1 one generation deeper, and it is now load-bearing rather than incidental, because v44 elevates the cumulative property from an implicit expectation to a GOVERNING rule and then does not meet it. A G22 implementation can satisfy all 47 named vectors and the GOVERNING roster rule as written while testing none of the arm64 zimg cardinality, compression-agreement, decompression-boundary, Kconfig-completeness or PE-decoy refusals that v37-v40 made mandatory and that v44's live text still requires. The declared rule also becomes unenforceable in practice: the first artifact it governs is the first artifact that does not satisfy it, so no successor can be measured against it.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Either (a) extend /g22/ikconfigParserVectors to the union across every predecessor roster that named required vectors (v37 through v43), adding at minimum: raw-PE decoy pair refuse; omitted requiredN refuse; six-line IKCONFIG decoy refuse; duplicate CONFIG_NAME refuse; arm64 duplicate zimg refuse; compressed_type/magic disagreement refuse; arm64 magic-free fallback refuse; unsupported-compression refuse; concatenated gzip and trailing-bytes refuse; malformed official header refuse; PE entrypoint-outside-loaded-executable-section refuse; signed ikconfigDigest mismatch refuse; or (b) issue an explicit named semantic withdrawal for each v37-v40 vector not carried forward, stating for each why it is obsolete, in the form used for kexecSymbolAbsence. Option (b) is unavailable for any vector whose rule remains live in the subject, which on the evidence above is all of them. Additionally, correct the caption 'union of v42 and v43' and the closing sentence 'No vector from v42 or v43 is withdrawn here' so that the scope of the roster matches the scope of the rule that governs it.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 2 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. Custody is clean, the closed-roster claim is mechanically verified with no silent path, the pinned v43 verdicts are correctly recorded, every authority guardrail holds, and the v42-union-v43 claim is true as stated. The subject nevertheless fails on the substance of the repair it exists to make: PTCB-V44-S1 shows one explicitly enumerated item of Codex's requiredRepair undelivered and conceded in the subject's own repair note, and PTCB-V44-S2 shows the newly declared GOVERNING cumulative-roster rule unsatisfied by the very roster it governs, which is the PTCB-V43-S1 failure mode recurring one generation deeper. Both are mechanically demonstrable from the subject's own text and are repairable by naming vectors; neither requires redesign.
